name: Dynamic Cheatsheet (DC): Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
venue: EACL 2026 (main conference, long paper; ACL Anthology 2026.eacl-long.333). First released as arXiv:2504.07952 (cs.LG/cs.CL), Apr 2025.
authors_affiliation: Mirac Suzgun, Mert Yuksekgonul, Federico Bianchi, Dan Jurafsky, James Zou. Primary affiliation: Stanford University (James Zou Lab; Suzgun acknowledges an HAI-SAP Fellowship).
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/suzgunmirac/dynamic-cheatsheet (actively maintained; last push 2026-03-12; 272 stars; MIT license; adds DynamicCheatsheet_CumulativeRetrieval hybrid variant and many new model providers beyond the v1 paper)
task_domain: Reasoning / math / QA / code-via-tool-use / decision-making at inference time. Tasks span competition math (AIME), graduate-level science QA (GPQA-Diamond, MMLU-Pro), and heuristic-search arithmetic puzzles (Game of 24, Math Equation Balancer).
problem_setting: Online, test-time / inference-time learning for a black-box LLM over a stream of i.i.d. queries x1..xn ~ D_test, with NO ground-truth labels, NO human feedback, and NO weight updates. Single-agent (one black-box LM plays both Generator and Curator roles via different prompts). The model must self-assess correctness and decide what to store. Sequential processing (one query at a time, carrying an evolving memory M_i forward).
what_is_retrieved: Self-curated reusable problem-solving artifacts: strategies, solution sketches, code snippets (e.g. a Python brute-force solver), heuristics, and general insights stored in an evolving text 'cheatsheet' memory. In the retrieval variant (DC-RS / DR), it retrieves past (input, model-generated output) pairs from previously seen examples.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory that the agent itself writes at test time. There is NO static external corpus, KB, or document index; the store is entirely induced online from the model's own past queries and self-curated solutions. (Explicitly contrasted with classic static-corpus RAG.)
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking in the retrieval variants (k=3 most similar past input-output pairs by cosine similarity). The cumulative variant (DC-Cu) has no ranking objective at all; the memory itself is the (single) reused artifact. No notion of recovering a complete minimal set or precision-driven variable-size selection.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve (DC-RS/DR retrieve similar past cases), Reuse (Generator conditions on memory/retrieved cases), Revise (Curator distills/refines/prunes entries; can correct faulty heuristics), Retain (Curator writes distilled artifacts to memory). All four CBR phases are realized in DC-RS; DC-Cu covers Reuse/Revise/Retain without explicit similarity Retrieve. Flags: [Retrieve: yes (DC-RS/DR), Reuse: yes, Revise: yes, Retain: yes].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work frames itself as 'test-time learning with adaptive memory' / 'persistent evolving memory' inspired by human cumulative learning and retrieval-practice (Karpicke & Roediger) and online learning; it does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner or call itself case-based reasoning, though DC-RS/DR realize CBR-like retrieve-reuse-revise-retain mechanics over (problem, solution) cases.
retrieval_unit: Case = (problem, model-generated solution) pair, i.e. past input-output examples (DC-RS / DR). The cumulative memory itself is a distilled set of strategy/heuristic/code-snippet entries (skill-or-program / guideline). Granularity: single past example (for retrieval) and distilled snippet/strategy (for the curated cheatsheet).
index_source: Growing memory, online/test-time-induced. The retrievable store of (x_j, y~_j) pairs and the curated cheatsheet are both built entirely at test time from the model's own stream of queries and self-generated solutions; nothing is induced offline and nothing is a static corpus.
index_structure_topology: Flat. DC-RS uses a flat vector index over past query embeddings (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small). The curated cheatsheet (DC-Cu) is a single flat free-text memory blob. Authors note hierarchical/modular memory and topological clustering only as future work, not implemented.
retriever_type: Dense embedding similarity (cosine) using OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small to embed raw input queries, then top-k nearest neighbors. Off-the-shelf; no trained retriever. (DC-Cu has no retriever.)
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The embedding model and cosine top-k are fixed; the retriever is not trained or fine-tuned on similarity labels, LM feedback, task effectiveness, or RL.
query_construction: Raw input query (the raw question text) is embedded directly as the query/key. No decomposition, sub-query generation, intent extraction, or thought-conditioning. For the Generator, the prompt is augmented with the current memory M_i (and, in DC-RS, the curator has already folded retrieved cases into M_i).
query_granularity: Task-level / one-shot per query. One retrieval (and one curation) is performed per incoming query x_i; there is no per-reasoning-step or trajectory-level sub-querying within a single problem.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot per query (DC-RS / DR): a single top-k retrieval is performed once when each new query arrives, before generation. DC-Cu performs no retrieval. Not iterative/active/uncertainty-triggered within a query.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval (when used, in DC-RS/DR) fires deterministically once per incoming query. No confidence/uncertainty/attention signal, learned router, or agent-initiated trigger decides whether to retrieve.
reranking: None. Retrieved items are the raw top-k=3 by cosine similarity with no reranking stage (no cross-encoder, RRF, or hierarchy-aware reranking).
retrieved_context_refinement: In DC-RS: the LLM Curator synthesizes/distills retrieved past (input, output) pairs together with the prior memory into a refined cheatsheet BEFORE generation (decompose-then-recompose / distillation). In DR baseline: none (retrieved pairs are pasted verbatim). The curation step also consolidates and prunes for clarity/compactness, acting as compression.
tool_document_engineering: N/A. Items retrieved are past query-solution pairs, not tool/API documents; there is no tool-description engineering. (Note: stored snippets can be executable Python code the model later reuses, but these are self-generated, not indexed tool docs.)
index_content_separation: No. The retrievable embedding key (query embedding) and the stored content (the past output / the cheatsheet text) are not split into a lightweight index plus on-demand heavy content; the curated memory is loaded into the prompt directly. Authors suggest a structured external database as future work.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A. No external tool index or integration protocol (no RapidAPI/REST/MCP/function-calling tool registry). The only 'tool' is a Python interpreter for executing model-written code (execute_python_code flag in the released code).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A. No inter-tool dependency modeling; the framework does not retrieve tools and has no dependency graph.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation + skill/case reuse. The current memory M_i (and, in DC-RS, the freshly synthesized cheatsheet incorporating retrieved cases) is injected into the Generator's prompt; the model reuses or adapts stored strategies/code snippets to solve the new query. No training signal and no parameter updates (black-box).
planning_integration: One-shot exemplars/strategies at solve time (plan time). For DC-Cu: generate-then-curate (solve using memory, then update memory). For DC-RS: retrieve-then-curate-then-generate (retrieve similar cases -> Curator refines memory -> Generator solves). Retrieval is woven in at the per-query level, not inside a tree search or per-reasoning-step loop. Optionally Python code execution provides a verify-by-execution step within a query (max_num_rounds, default 1).
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer / per-query. Retrieval and memory update happen once around the full solution to each query; not interleaved per-CoT-step, per-sentence/token, or per-tool-call (aside from the optional single code-execution round).
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation + execution-feedback. The Curator (an LLM prompted task-agnostically) distills/revises retrieved cases and prior memory into reusable strategies; stored code snippets can be re-executed (Python interpreter) so execution feedback influences which solutions are trusted and retained. Reuse is via in-context conditioning, not RL fine-tuning.
retrieved_item_representation: Mixed: distilled strategies/heuristics/insights as free text, plus executable Python code snippets, plus (in DC-RS/DR) raw past (input, output) example pairs. The curated cheatsheet is a structured-ish free-text note focused on concise, transferable snippets rather than full transcripts.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Two levels: (1) distilled strategy/insight/heuristic and procedural skill (reusable Python program) in the cumulative cheatsheet; (2) raw past single demonstration (problem+solution case) in the retrieval variants. Spans from concrete code-skill to abstract guideline.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Self-curation/self-reflection by the Curator (assesses usefulness/generalizability, refines or prunes faulty entries, consolidates for compactness) without ground-truth labels; optional Python code execution to validate code-based solutions. Authors explicitly flag retrieval noise as a weakness (e.g. GPT-4o on GPQA-Diamond degraded from suboptimal retrieved cases) and note no advanced relevance filtering is used beyond cosine top-k.
memory_type: Episodic + skill-library hybrid, realized as a single non-parametric, evolving free-text memory ('cheatsheet'): stores past cases/experiences (episodic) and distilled reusable strategies + code skills (skill-library/procedural).
write_back: True. The Curator writes distilled strategies, code snippets, and insights back into the memory after (DC-Cu) or before (DC-RS) generation: M_{i+1} = Cur(M_i, x_i, y~_i).
online_growth: Yes. The memory and the retrievable pool of past (input, output) pairs grow continuously during deployment/test-time; nothing is frozen after offline induction. (Memory is also consolidated/pruned, so it grows in content but is kept compact.)
write_back_trigger: Reflective, every query (after self-critique). The Curator runs once per query and decides what to add/refine/prune based on its own assessment of the solution's correctness, usefulness, and generalizability (no human validation, no ground-truth gating). It is not strictly on-success-only: it may also revise or prune entries judged faulty.
failure_experience_usage: Partial / corrective. The Curator may revise or remove faulty heuristics judged incorrect or superseded, so failed/incorrect content can trigger pruning. However the framework is biased toward retaining correct/useful strategies (self-assessed without labels); it does not maintain an explicit success+failure contrastive store. Authors note faulty heuristics can slip in and be amplified.
memory_evolution_update: Refine-overwrite + dedup/consolidate + forget-prune. Stored entries are mutated after writing: the Curator distills, consolidates for compactness/clarity, updates entries superseded by better strategies, and prunes incorrect ones (not append-only). FH baseline is the append-only contrast.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Case selection is fixed cosine top-k similarity (off-the-shelf embeddings), not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy. The 'learning' is in the LLM-curated memory content, not in a trained selection policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Primarily single-agent private memory. The paper briefly explores transferring curated memory from a larger model to a smaller one (cross-model), with mixed/limited results, but there is no collective multi-agent shared memory; deployment is single-agent per task stream.
benchmarks: AIME 2024 (30 q), AIME 2025 (30 q), AIME 2020-2024 (133 q), GPQA-Diamond (198 q), Game of 24 (100 examples from Suzgun & Kalai 2024), Math Equation Balancer (250 expressions, authors' own), MMLU-Pro Engineering (250 sampled) and MMLU-Pro Physics (250 sampled).
benchmark_family: QA (GPQA-Diamond, MMLU-Pro), competition-math reasoning (AIME), and heuristic-search / arithmetic puzzles (Game of 24, Math Equation Balancer). No web/embodied/tool-retrieval/code-repo/memory-dialog (LoCoMo) or decision-RL (D4RL) benchmarks.
baselines: BL (vanilla baseline prompting, one-off inference), DC-empty (DC-0, structured problem-solving + Python tool-use instructions but memory kept empty; strong baseline), FH (Full-History Appending; all past input-output pairs verbatim, no curation), DR (Dynamic Retrieval; retrieve top-k similar past pairs pasted verbatim, no curation/synthesis), and Majority Voting (MV, 3 generations). Also zero-shot CoT was tried in preliminary experiments (no gain, not included).
key_metrics: Task accuracy (%): Soft Match (SM) for multiple-choice GPQA-Diamond and MMLU-Pro; Functionally Correct (FC) for Game of 24, Math Equation Balancer, and AIME. Also reports cumulative-accuracy progression curves and average output tokens (efficiency).
headline_result: GPT-4o's Game of 24 success rate rose from ~10% (baseline) to 99% under DC-RS after it discovered and reused a Python brute-force solver. Other headline gains: Claude 3.5 Sonnet AIME 2024 23.3% -> 50.0% (DC-Cu, +27 pts, more than doubled); AIME 2025 6.7% -> 36.7% (DC-Cu); GPQA-Diamond 59.6% -> 68.7% (DC-RS, +9.1); MMLU-Pro Physics 74% -> 82% (+8); Math Equation Balancer ~45-50% -> 98-100%.
ablations: DC-empty (DC-0) isolates memory effect (Game of 24: GPT-4o 19% vs 99% DC-RS, showing memory/reuse is the driver). DR vs DC-RS isolates curation/synthesis vs raw verbatim retrieval (GPQA-Diamond Sonnet: DR 63.6% vs DC-RS 68.7%). FH vs DC isolates curation vs append-everything (AIME 2024 Sonnet: FH 26.7% vs DC-Cu 50.0%; GPT-4o FH dropped to 6.7-13.3% below baseline). MV comparison (no gain over BL). top-k sensitivity (k=3 vs 5/7 -> negligible gain). Model-scale ablation (Claude 3.5 Haiku, GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek R1/o1 show muted/inconsistent gains). Cross-model memory transfer (mixed). Example-ordering / task-similarity (curriculum) amplifies gains.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task accuracy is reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval completeness) are reported separately. Retrieval quality is discussed only qualitatively (e.g. suboptimal retrieved cases hurting GPQA-Diamond).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final-answer accuracy). Some process-level insight is offered qualitatively (cumulative-accuracy curves over the stream, inspection of curated memory contents, token-usage trends, error/correction clustering in embedding space) but no quantitative step-wise reasoning or retrieval accuracy.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reports average output tokens on AIME 2024 for Claude 3.5 Sonnet: BL 370, DC-0 494, DC-RS 1035, DC-Cu 1831 tokens. DC incurs per-query curation overhead and an initial discovery cost, but amortizes by avoiding re-deriving solutions (e.g. reusing a stored Python solver), reducing redundant computation over time. Sequential structure limits batch parallelism. No dollar cost or latency numbers reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Retrieval fixed at top-k=3 (default; k=5/7 gave negligible gain). Generation max_tokens default 2048 (released code). Memory is budget-controlled implicitly by Curator-driven consolidation/compactness rather than a hard token cap, explicitly to avoid context ballooning vs the FH (append-all) baseline.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a method paper, not a survey/taxonomy).
benchmark_construction_and_size: Math Equation Balancer is authors'-constructed (250 arithmetic expressions, e.g. '1 ? 2 ? 3 = 6'); Game of 24 uses 100 examples from Suzgun & Kalai (2024); AIME subsets and GPQA-Diamond/MMLU-Pro are existing public datasets (sizes: AIME 30/30/133, GPQA-Diamond 198, MMLU-Pro 250 each subset sampled). Answers are verifiable via Functionally Correct / Soft Match metrics. The paper is method-centric, not a benchmark paper.
builds_on: Retrieval-augmented generation (REALM/Guu et al. 2020; RAG-style retrieval) and in-context learning; self-reflective retrieval (Self-RAG, Asai et al. 2023); test-time/online adaptation lineage (dynamic evaluation, Krause et al. 2019; domain-adaptive pretraining, Gururangan et al. 2020); LLM reasoning/search (Tree-of-Thoughts Yao et al. 2023, Graph-of-Thoughts); STaR-style self-improvement (Zelikman et al. 2022); human retrieval-practice/cumulative-learning psychology (Karpicke & Roediger).
contrasts_with: Fine-tuning / gradient-based parameter updates; static-corpus retrieval-augmented generation (retrieving facts from a fixed external KB); naive full-history appending (FH); raw verbatim retrieval without curation (DR); and majority voting / self-consistency (passive aggregation). DC instead curates a compact, evolving, self-generated memory of strategies/code at test time, leaving black-box weights untouched.
lineage: Group F (F_decision_memory_rl): test-time / experience-driven memory methods. Sits in the lineage of agent/LM experience-memory methods where a GROWING self-written memory of strategies/cases (rather than a static document corpus) is retrieved and reused; the DC-RS variant adds episodic case retrieval (top-k similar past (problem, solution) pairs), bridging cumulative skill-library memory and CBR-style case reuse.
